symbols.meaning: The Fool stands outside the sequence of the Major Arcana. He can appear anywhere and belongs to every stage of the journey.
All he owns travels with him. It shows experience carried lightly and a life not tied to one place.

symbols.where: in his hand, touching the ground
symbols.meaning: His support on the road and his link to the earth even while he wanders.
Instinct nipping at his heels: a warning, a companion, or the past trying to hold him back.
The jester's dress, free to speak truth and laugh at convention.
Cups, coins, a knife and dice: the four suits and every possibility laid out ready to use.
He links the spiritual and the material, the idea and its result.
Its brim curves like the sign of infinity, showing boundless creative potential. Strength wears the same hat.
A fourth leg is unseen. Not everything is shown; something remains hidden or still to be built.
New growth, the first sprouts of what he is beginning.
Sacred knowledge being studied. Wisdom here is read slowly and absorbed over time.
Spiritual authority held by a woman, the sacred feminine as keeper of mysteries.
Something is hidden and not yet revealed. She guards the threshold of the unknown.
Many layers of meaning, as in a text read again and again.
Her protective power and her ability to rise above, guarding what she creates.
Authority over the material world, power used to make things grow.
Creative spirit lifting earthly power, imagination with the strength to rule.
Open, confident and fully present, she shows herself without hiding.
His legs form the shape of the number four, the figure of stability and order.
Protection and power that rests on the ground, ready but not raised.
His authority to rule, set laws and defend.
He looks toward the world he governs, attention turned outward to his responsibilities.
The weight and honor of office, power bound to duty.
He passes spiritual blessing to others; the glove shows the sacredness of his role.
Authority across body, mind and spirit, or the three worlds.
Students or seekers who receive his teaching. We stand where they stand.
The structure of tradition and the gateway between sacred and everyday life.
The one who must choose, pulled between two paths or two loves.
Often read as duty and desire, or the old bond and the new. Each seems to claim him.
Love that comes from above and decides beyond reason. The arrow will strike.
The pull of influence and expectation in matters of the heart.
Opposing forces that must be held together and moved in one direction.
He steers by will and presence, not by force.
Different moods or aspects of the self, all carried and mastered.
Protection and a link to higher purpose as he moves forward.
A solid, earthly base for his victory.
Gentle control of instinct. She opens or closes the jaws without struggle.
The same infinity-shaped brim as the Magician, linking willpower to inner strength.
Raw passion and instinct that cooperates when met with patience.
In the Marseille order Strength begins the second half of the Major Arcana.
Inner light and hard-won wisdom, partly shielded and shared only with true seekers.
Support for a long journey and the patience of age.
Withdrawal from the world, privacy and protection for the inner search.
Nine written as four ones and a five, the old Marseille way. Completion and wisdom.
Life's cycles turning. Someone or something unseen keeps it moving.
Fortune on the way up, effort and ambition.
Fortune going down, loss and humility.
The moment of balance at the peak, wisdom and judgment above the turning.
Clear decision and the cutting away of falsehood.
Weighing both sides fairly and finding balance.
Justice that sees clearly. She is not blindfolded here.
The law and structure that frame her judgment.
In the Marseille order Justice is eight, the number of balance.
A deliberate change of perspective. He sees the world upside down.
Stillness and a pose of chosen surrender.
Growth paused. Something has been pruned so something new can come.
He does not act; he waits and receives.
The force of ending and clearing, which reaps what is finished.
No rank escapes change. Even kings must let go.
Old ways of doing and old paths cut away.
New life already growing from what was cleared.
The card is left unnamed, showing respect for its power and mystery.
Opposites being blended: spirit and matter, feeling and thought.
Healing flow and moderation; nothing is spilled.
A messenger between heaven and earth bringing grace.
Gentle beauty and growth through patience.
Raw desire and instinctive power, both creative and binding.
People bound by attachment. Their ropes are loose enough to remove.
Passion that can light the way or burn.
The material world he rules, and the attachments built on it.

symbols.where: striking the crown of the tower
symbols.meaning: Sudden revelation from above that breaks false structures open.
Pride and false authority knocked loose.
Being shaken out of old certainties.
Blessings or energy released by the breakthrough.
The divine entering the house; disruption as a sacred event.
Hope, guidance and renewal shining after darkness.
The traditional planets or the many lights that guide.
Giving to the earth and the waters; generosity and healing.
Openness and honesty with nothing hidden.
The soul and inspiration resting nearby.
Reflected light and partial seeing; the unconscious.
Energy drawn upward, dreams and longing.
The tame and wild instincts responding to the moon.
The gateway into the unknown.
Deep, primitive feelings rising from the unconscious.
Consciousness, warmth and life-giving clarity.
Blessings and energy raining down.
Friendship, partnership and innocent joy.
A safe, protected space where joy can flourish.
The call to awaken and rise.
Spiritual victory and renewal.
Rebirth of the whole self, body, mind and spirit.
The one who answers the call; we take their place.
Wholeness in motion; completion that keeps living.
The cycle completed, a protective circle of victory.
Angel, eagle, lion and bull: the four elements and the four evangelists, all united.
Will and power carried lightly at the end of the journey.
